_comment: Per-scene floors for tools/perceptual_gate.py, calibrated 2026-09-20 from
measurement, not invented. Two sources:
(a) the exact-reference build against itself in the two configurations
it already ships -- golden (--interp, --quantum 128, serial) against
default (--quantum 0, threads). Most scenes are byte-identical; the
spread comes from the interleave, and it is the floor of variation
a build we fully trust already produces.
(b) sm64 golden against --timing-oc: mean 0.9999, p01 0.9960, min 0.9760.
SUPERSEDED 2026-09-20 -- see the sm64 note below. That run had the
geometry worker on, because the frontends wire --timing-oc to it,
so it did not measure the model Phase 1 installs.
Measured (a), all 1800 frames unless noted:
sm64 / dbori / mlbis / meteos / gsdd(300)  exact
artacd   mean 1.0000  p01 1.0000  min 0.9981  psnr min 40.9
etody    mean 1.0000  p01 0.9998  min 0.9772  psnr min 39.0  (223 realigned)
st-intro mean 0.9998  p01 0.9983  min 0.9970  psnr min 41.0  (600 frames)
sm64, recalibrated 2026-09-20 (Phase 1a). The row above was set from (b),
which ran the geometry worker; 1a deletes the worker on the evidence in
the plan's SS3.4, and the no-worker model measures mean 0.9981, p01
0.9509, min 0.9146, psnr mean 94.2 -- 1647/1800 frames exact, 677
realigned, one transient region frame and no persistent structural fault.
The four worst frames were rendered before the floor was touched
(fixtures/golden/evidence/): at the global minimum, frame 1229 at ssim
0.9146, the castle, the file menu, the water and every button are
pixel-identical and the whole difference is the TOUCH TO START text and
two bouncing arrows caught at a different point in their pulse. Frame
1002, the largest at 4.61 % of pixels, is the logo's sparkle trail a few
sprites further along, the same text at a different blink phase, and a
one-frame rotation of Mario's head showing as a thin outline. What the
metric reports here is animation phase, not picture quality: the elements
move fast enough that no whole-frame shift in the +/-2 window lines them
up. Floors moved to p01 0.940 and min 0.900, which still sit below the
measurement with headroom; the structural faults are unchanged and remain
the real gate.
The metric floors are deliberately looser than those numbers: they exist to
catch gradual degradation across a phase, while the structural faults --
which no floor excuses and which are checked separately -- catch the
failures that actually matter. Tighten a scene's row when a phase lands
and the measurement supports it; never loosen one without recording why.
